problem: Existing VLN models, including persistent-scene IVLN methods, degrade sharply when one long instruction describes several chained navigation sub-tasks, because too much instruction text hinders grounding to the current observation. Long trajectories also let early errors compound, and prior methods have no error-correction mechanism.
motivation: Real deployments ask an agent to do several sequential tasks in one large, persistent scene from one instruction. Directly applying large LLMs is impractical on-device and lacks scene knowledge. Long instructions are naturally ordered phrase sequences, so matching phrases to the current view and exploiting their order can reduce load and detect errors.
key_idea: Use hierarchical planning: a CLIP-plus-entropy high-level planner picks the phrase of the long instruction relevant to the current view, and a low-level planner switches between exploration and verification modes that use phrase-order consistency to backtrack errors.
insight: Segmenting instructions helps small LLMs a lot: a 0.5B encoder with ISM (val-unseen SR 30, t-nDTW 45) beats 7B and 13B encoders without ISM (SR 27, t-nDTW 41 and 42). Entropy gating (peak at threshold 0.65) beats always taking the max-similarity phrase (SR 27), since ambiguous cases need the global instruction. Period-based segmentation works best (SR 30 vs 23 unsegmented). The EaV ablation shows both verification terms help: without verification SR is 25, and with both terms it is 30, at the cost of a longer trajectory.
method: Instruction Segmentation Module (ISM): CLIP ViT-B/32 (frozen) encodes each phrase and the current RGB view; cosine similarities go through a softmax over phrases; the argmax phrase is used if the distribution's entropy is below threshold 0.65, otherwise the global instruction is used.
Instruction encoder: Qwen-0.5B embeds either the selected phrase or the global instruction (alpha switch); the last hidden state is the instruction embedding.

Scene Mapping Module and Map-Encoder: persistent semantic (13-channel) and occupancy maps are cropped around the agent, then encoded by 4 CBRA blocks (conv k=7, BN, ReLU, avg-pool, spatial attention) into a 128x4x4 embedding, following IVLN.
Action Output Head: two GRUs with cross-attention take map embedding, instruction embedding, previous hidden state and previous action, and output FORWARD 0.25m / TURN 15° / STOP.

Exploration-Verification (EaV): when the newly selected phrase is not the successor of the last one (Term-I) and the CLIP similarity between the view and the next phrase is below threshold delta_0 (Term-II), the agent turns back one step and takes the second-best action.

Adaptive verification threshold: delta_0 starts at 0.30, decreases 0.01 per 10 actions and 0.05 on a failed verification, increases 0.03 on success, with a floor of 0.05. It outperforms fixed thresholds.

SH IR2R-CE benchmark: IR2R-CE trajectories with matching endpoints are stitched, their instructions merged with LLaMA, and each phrase enriched with visual details by LLaVA-OneVision from the ground-truth trajectory views. Two new metrics are added: CPsubT (completed sub-task ratio) and CPsubI (correct sub-instruction selection).

setting.backbone: Qwen-0.5B instruction encoder (trained) + frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 + Map-Encoder CNN + GRU action head (trained)
setting.training_data: SH IR2R-CE (the authors' stitched and LLM-enriched IR2R-CE) for SH-VLN; IR2R-CE for the IVLN table; two-stage imitation (teacher forcing, then fine-tuning) with progress monitor loss
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with persistent semantic + occupancy maps
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT 15° / TURN RIGHT 15° / STOP
setting.privileged: none stated beyond IVLN-style map building (semantic maps)

results: On the new SH IR2R-CE benchmark SeqWalker gets val-unseen SR 30 and t-nDTW 45, versus the best baseline MAP-CMA (SR 23, t-nDTW 39) and HNR (SR 21). On the standard IR2R-CE it reaches val-unseen SR 36, SPL 34 and t-nDTW 52, ahead of OVER-NAV (SR 35, SPL 33, t-nDTW 50), a small margin.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulated indoor Habitat scenes with a self-built, LLM-generated benchmark; no real-robot tests and no generalization to outdoor scenes.

Verification adds trajectory length, and CLIP-based phrase matching with hand-tuned entropy/segmentation heuristics may be brittle, since the best segmentation is the dataset's period-delimited style.
Baselines are retrained on the authors' dataset, and the IR2R-CE gain over OVER-NAV is small.
